names.name: Dipping and sprinkles
names.said: New England says jimmies. Almost nowhere else does.

text.what: Icing in flat pans, sprinkles in bins: a donut is dipped face-down, then set in the sprinkles while the icing is still wet.
text.story: Sprinkles are small pieces of confectionery used as decoration. The long ones are called jimmies in parts of the United States, above all New England and Philadelphia; the tiny balls are nonpareils. Chocolate, maple, strawberry and vanilla icings are the standard dips, and the colour on a shop's sprinkles is one of the few things it chooses purely to look like itself.
text.how: Dip, lift, tilt to shed the excess, then straight into the tray of sprinkles before it sets.
text.today: A case of sprinkled donuts is the shop's shop window, which is why the bright ones sit at eye level.
